mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP growth (measured by the quarterly change in GDPC1) signals robust economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following quarters with positive GDPC1 growth (quarterly change > 0) and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% over the past three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following months where UNRATE has increased by more than 0.5 percentage points over the prior three months and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and an increase in the consumer price index above 3.5% signals a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically leads to a temporary market correction as investors reassess growth and inflation risks, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following the joint condition (FEDFUNDS < 3.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%) and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, high housing starts (HOUST) and strong retail sales (RSAFS) signal excessive consumer spending, which increases the likelihood of a Fed rate hike and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following the late-cycle expansion regime (HOUST > 1500 and RSAFS > 750000) and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index above 3.5% year-over-year signals persistent inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following months with CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5% and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by a high level of employment (PAYEMS), supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following months with PAYEMS above 150000 and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals a weakening economy, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following the joint condition (INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 4.0) and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of supply chain disruption, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 and a concurrent rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4.0% signal a contractionary supply shock, which increases inflation and reduces economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the 5-day periods following the supply shock regime (INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 4.0) and the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.
